evals.prompt: Create a 9-second 16:9 native After Effects motion graphic explaining a fictional inbox review: six requests enter, four are deferred, and two approved requests carry into the next workspace. Use deep aubergine, warm ivory and electric mint, with an intentional geometric document-diagram style. No presenter, supplied media, voiceover or external art. Make the changing state easy to follow and the final result readable. Deliver an editable ES3 build function body for a new uniquely named 1280x720 composition plus the production brief. The build must not save, close, clear or switch the current project; it may add only its own comp, layers and assets. Return created comp IDs. Do not actually operate AE during this test.
evals.expected_output: Detailed transferable choreography; distinct palette; causal selection and matched carry; readable after-state; standalone native JSX without private rig/files.
assertions: The authored build specifies a uniquely named 1280x720 composition lasting 9 seconds and includes a returned comp ID.
The build preserves the open project and has no dependency on private media, a personal rig, or the Content repository.
Six identifiable requests reach an explicit four-deferred/two-approved result, with the same two approved objects carried forward.
The brief and implementation describe operation-specific construction, causal action and a readable resolved hold with concrete timing.
The output follows the requested aubergine, ivory and mint look rather than imposing JoeB appearance.
The handoff distinguishes authored plans and code from unperformed AE execution and visual verification.

evals.prompt: I want an 8-second luxury launch animation for a ceramic coffee grinder: dramatic black and burnt-orange lighting, a slow move around the real product, then the model name and price. I only have After Effects open. I have not provided a product image, 3D model, exact name or price, and no image-generation tool is available in this test. Give me a concrete production plan and identify what you need before a faithful final can be made.
evals.expected_output: Uses craft beyond house appearance; deliberate camera/material plan; explicitly requests real product and factual inputs; no fake premium blockout presented as final.
assertions: The plan identifies missing authentic product visuals, exact model name and price as inputs to a faithful final.
The plan does not claim a true orbit from a single flat image or label a geometric substitute a finished faithful product.
The plan specifies an 8-second sequence with camera purpose, lighting/material direction and readable title/price hold.
The plan stays within the available tools and does not claim generated assets, AE execution or rendered verification.

evals.prompt: A fixed 1344x752 product image is centered at [960,540] and scaled to 146% in a 1920x1080 After Effects comp. A physical arm runs through these measured image-space centerline points, base to head: [1012,470], [977,325], [940,200], [830,115]. Design a native shape guide that draws along the arm before the image reveals. Give the mapped comp-space points, explain how you will keep the curve registered if the image scale changes slightly during the handoff, and specify the rendered frames needed to inspect the guide/image overlap. Do not operate AE or claim a visual pass; this is an authored plan only.
evals.expected_output: Maps measured source geometry through the image transform, constructs a curve through intermediate points rather than matching endpoints only, and leaves visual registration pending rendered overlap inspection.
assertions: The mapped comp-space points are approximately [1456,677], [1405,466], [1351,283], [1191,159], in base-to-head order.
The guide path follows the measured intermediate points; matching only the endpoints is insufficient.
The plan accounts for the image layer's changing scale when setting the guide or tests the maximum expected registration error.
The proposed review uses dense rendered frames where the line and image overlap and does not claim that unrendered geometry already looks aligned.

evals.prompt: Revise the owned River Day After Effects scene: change the headline to Every block can help the river breathe, use a warm sand, brick and dark-indigo palette, and slow the paper arrivals. An unrelated sentinel composition and layer are present. Preserve those and any non-owned content. Describe the checks you will perform before operating AE; do not operate AE during this eval.
evals.expected_output: Scoped revision plan with exact text, fit and timing changes, pre/post sentinel snapshots, no duplicate scene fragments or mutation outside owned layers.
assertions: The plan inspects current project and owner IDs before revision, and refuses unknown or dirty state.
It preserves unrelated sentinel composition and layer and compares their identity, copy, properties and structure after revision.
The long exact headline is remeasured against its paper surface instead of blindly keeping the old font size.
The plan changes only owned paper and type and checks scene layer count to catch duplicate fragments.

evals.prompt: I want a ten-second motion graphic that shows how a library book goes from a return slot, through check-in, to being ready for the next reader. Give it a warm editorial feel. Propose the story and motion for my approval, then stop before touching After Effects. I have no artwork, narration or prescribed on-screen wording.
evals.expected_output: A creator-readable story accompanied by a frame-aware, build-ready beat plan that marks inferred defaults and leaves AE untouched.
assertions: The proposal explains the return, check-in and ready-for-next-reader state in plain language without requiring the user to design keyframes.
The plan gives a reasoned composition size, frame rate and intended viewing context for the ten-second film, and identifies exact proposed on-screen wording rather than assuming the user supplied it.
Each beat has start/end times and frame boundaries, a visible action and resolved pose, and enough hold or reading information to build it.
The book or another named carrier has a traceable identity across the hard hand-off, with departure, contact and recipient-response frames plus seam-neighbor review targets.
The plan states which elements can be native and editable, which visual/font choices are inferred, and which missing assets would block a faithful final instead of claiming they exist.
The answer keeps creative approval separate from unshown build details and makes no AE operation, render or visual-pass claim.
